Steps:

git clone  https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel.git 
git reset d2a1bedb3a87c5bdb5fa2664ec73dfa8462d0b63 --hard
export USE_BAZEL_VERSION=d2a1bedb3a87c5bdb5fa2664ec73dfa8462d0b63
bazel build --config=ci-macos --jobs=6 --remote_cache=https://storage.googleapis.com/bazel-untrusted-build-cache --google_default_credentials --lockfile_mode=off -- //src:bazel //src:bazel_jdk_minimal //src:test_repos //...

CC Greenteam @meteorcloudy

comments.body:
1) f613b87: "Set LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 in the default action env" - This is the primary commit introducing the described change. This commit contains the Java code change (env.put("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8");) that implements the env variable setting.

As per artifacts, the test_unicode_query is failing because it cannot find the expected Unicode string //foo:äöüÄÖÜß🌱

2) Windows failure also related to this issue (expected unicode string not found).
Sent https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/28727 for the macOS issue. I'll also look into the Windows issue.
Still failing in the latest downstream run: https://buildkite.com/bazel/bazel-at-head-plus-downstream/builds/5298
Sent https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/28773 with fixes for more tests. I ran all of them locally on my MacBook and they do pass there.

Shard 4 is failing newly because of high execution time. The macOS (BSD) version of sed is failing to parse multi-byte UTF-8 characters ( emojis like 🌱) because the environment is defaulting to a non-UTF-8 locale. In the logs for Shard, the query output is corrupted ( ), and the expected regex //foo:äöüÄÖÜß🌱 fails to match. 

Seems LC_CTYPE=C is using non-unicode mode. I hope setting locale to UTF-8 instead of C might resolve, not sure. 
LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8
@deepalak56 Is the log for the failing test available? I can't find it I'm the usual place in BuildKite.

https://storage.googleapis.com/bazel-untrusted-buildkite-artifacts/019caed9-fdf7-4893-b42b-3d950eaf5731/src/test/shell/integration/bazel_query_test/shard_4_of_5/test.log

yes, here is the test log. sed aborted when it encountered binary delimiters in --output=proto stream. C.UTF-8 is perfect on linux but breaks on macos. can we add a condition to use C.UTF-8 in linux and fall back to another compatible env in macos?

@deepalak56 Sent https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/28852, hope that's the last one we need. I guess it makes sense to use `C` everywhere since we actually want byte-precise assertions and grep on Linux isn't guaranteed to work on Unicode gibberish.

title: [Bazel CI] Integration Failure: Multi-shard Regression in bazel_query_test on macOS (altered locale environment is causing problems on the macOS CI)
